Donovan / team —

Attack simulation summary (ops-level): we ran a red-team style exercise against a staging instance that mirrors the Shared-VPC tenant topology. Sequence and controls:

1) Initial compromise: attacker obtains credentials in a tenant web app (simulated API key theft).
   - Control: tenant-facing ACLs, token rotation, rate limiting (prevents large scale data pulls).
2) Lateral movement attempt: attacker attempts to reach internal metadata and other tenant subnets via the tenant bridge.
   - Control: sidecar egress enforcement (per-container egress policy), per-tenant DNAT rules, and veth isolation. Sidecars enforce allowlists and TLS interception for outbound flows.
3) Privilege escalation: attacker tries to escalate via operator control plane (KMS/API).
   - Control: control plane strictly separated on a hardened management network; mutual TLS + mTLS client certs for operator APIs; operator ACLs only allow specific management hosts.
4) Exfiltration: attacker attempts to tunnel data over allowed egress (HTTPS) to an external host.
   - Control: egress proxy with header-based filtering, DLP hook (content indicators), and per-tenant bandwidth thresholds that triggered automated anomaly alerts.

Observed gaps and compensations: during a sidecar crash simulation we observed transient increases in allowed outbound SYN attempts until the kill-switch triggered (approx 12–18s). Compensations: enforced route blackhole on detection, short TTL for session tokens, and a failover proxy that enforces a strict deny-all until sidecar health is restored. We include logs showing the detection at 2027-05-11T14:12:22Z and the automated route change at 2027-05-11T14:12:35Z (in the attached zip).

Artifacts attached: shared-vpc-diagram.pdf (annotated), egress-policy-matrix.csv, attack-sim-results-20270511.zip (logs + pcap + timeline.md).

If Hearthbank would like, we can redact PII from the pcaps and provide a court-ready evidence set for auditors.

-ben

Donovan / Elena —

Attached is the evidence packet for your auditors. Summary and recommended next steps below so you have a single-sheet for the morning review:

Executive summary (2 bullets):
- Shared-VPC in our Dedicated/Private offering enforces per-tenant network micro-segmentation via operator-managed ENIs/virtual interfaces and sidecar-enforced egress policies. Control plane is on a separate management network with mTLS and KMS-backed key usage.
- Attack sim showed that layered controls (sidecar allowlists + egress proxy + control-plane ACLs + DLP hooks + automated route blackhole) prevent lateral escalation to operator systems and enable quick containment of exfiltration attempts.

Attachments (auditor view):
- shared-vpc-diagram.pdf — annotated with ACL/CIDR and operator plane demarcation
- egress-policy-matrix.csv — mapping rules to business justification (columns: rule_id, source_role, destination, justification, approval_owner)
- attack-sim-results-20270511.zip — zip contains: timeline.md, operator-logs.log, pcap-sample.pcap (redacted), and mitigation-scripts.sh (ops steps used to enact route blackhole)

Limitations & compensating controls (short):
- Fail-open sidecar crash window (~12–18s): mitigated via route blackhole + token TTLs + health-monitoring automation
- Human-dependent approvals for ad-hoc egress exceptions: we recommend a short SOP for emergency approval to avoid delayed incident response

Recommended actions for Hearthbank prior to onboarding:
1) Confirm egress allowlist domains and provide any additional DLP patterns you require.
2) Designate two emergency contacts for break-glass egress approval (we recommend SOC + network ops).
3) Optional: schedule a 45-minute tabletop with our security ops team to walk a response runbook using your specific playbooks (we can run this week of May 17).

Please let me know if you want any redaction on the artifacts before I share the Drive link with Elena for the auditor packet.

Thanks — we look forward to moving this to your compliance folder.
